overall: Atlanta is running significantly cooler than models expected, with the daily max stuck at 73.4°F since at least 7:00 AM — an unusually flat trend through the mid-afternoon. The current temperature of 69.8°F is actually below the running max, and velocity is flat at 0.0°F/hr, suggesting active suppression of warming likely driven by the very high dewpoint of 66.2°F (indicating thick boundary-layer moisture, cloud cover, or both). At 13:30 ET, we are approaching but not yet at peak heating hours (typically 2–5 PM), so some recovery is still possible, but the trend is discouraging.
forecast_obs_notes: Models are sharply split and all running well above observed reality: ECMWF at 77.0°F, HRRR at 75.5°F, and NBM at 79.2°F all require a 4–6°F+ surge from the current observed level in the remaining afternoon window, which is inconsistent with the zero-velocity flat trend. The Even ensemble model (74–75°F) aligns much better with observed conditions than the Odd model (81–82°F), and given the high moisture/suppression signal, the lower-end model suite appears far more credible today.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max frozen at 73.4°F through 13:30 ET and zero warming momentum, the burden of proof is on bulls — any significant jump would require a rapid clearing event in the next 1–2 hours. The most probable outcome is a modest afternoon recovery to the 74–76°F range, with 74–75°F carrying the highest probability weight given the Even model signal and observed suppression. Confidence is moderate-to-good that the day's high stays well below the NWS/NBM guidance of 79°F; a run toward 81–82°F (Odd model) is very unlikely barring a dramatic airmass shift not reflected in current conditions.
